name: Posedown / posing practice

lead: Posing practice is the rehearsal of bodybuilding poses, such as front and rear lat spreads, double biceps and side chest, so that muscle is shown with the best angles, tension and control. A posedown is the head-to-head posing round that follows judging.

It helps looks because the same physique can look noticeably more or less impressive depending on how it is presented. Information comes mostly from competition rules and training logs; no studies are listed.

paras: Competitors practise in front of a mirror or with a coach, running through mandatory poses and a personal routine. Training logs on T Nation mention bodybuilding posing sessions of about 40 minutes inside a training week.
Sustained isometric holds can cause cramping and fatigue. Posing itself is low risk; competition prep around it is a separate topic.

angle.text: Posing practice improves how existing muscle is displayed. Competitors rehearse mandatory poses and routines so their best angles are held with control.

lead: Posing practice is the rehearsal of the poses judged in bodybuilding. Wikipedia lists mandatory poses such as front and rear lat spreads, front and back double biceps, side chest, side triceps, abdominals and thighs, and a personal choreographed routine; a posedown typically takes place at the end of a posing round while judges finish scoring. [1]

The aim is to show a physique at its best. Wikipedia advises bodybuilders to practise posing extensively in front of a mirror or with a coach. [1] On T Nation, lifters mention folding posing into training, one listing 40 minutes of bodybuilding posing alongside lifting and conditioning, and others discuss posing trunks and Mr. Olympia posedowns. [2][3][4]
